subject: Critical Thinking
title: Validity vs. Soundness: When Logic Isn't Enough
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Validity vs. Soundness: When Logic Isn't Enough.

hook.text: 'All fish can fly. A salmon is a fish. Therefore, a salmon can fly.' The logic is perfect. The conclusion is absurd.

buildup.text: Validity: the conclusion follows logically from the premises.

discovery.text: The fish argument is valid but unsound. Good logic with bad inputs gives bad outputs.

twist.text: The reverse is also dangerous: true premises with invalid logic. 'Most Xs are Y. Z is Y.

climax.text: Strong arguments need BOTH: true premises (check facts) AND valid logic (check structure). Miss either, and you fail.

punchline.text: Perfect logic with false premises is still a lie. Just a well-structured one.

quiz.question: What makes an argument 'sound'?
options: It is spoken loudly and clearly
It is both logically valid AND has true premises

details.summary: A valid argument has a logical structure where the conclusion must follow if the premises are true. A sound argument is valid and also has true premises. Validity alone does not guarantee truth.
details.whyItMatters: Knowing the difference prevents you from accepting logically structured nonsense just because the form looks correct.
takeaways: Validity is about logical structure, not factual truth
Soundness requires both valid structure and true premises
An argument can be valid yet completely wrong

faq.question: Can an argument be valid but still have a false conclusion?
faq.answer: Yes. If the premises are false but the logical structure is correct, the argument is valid but unsound. The conclusion can be completely wrong despite perfect form.

faq.question: Why is soundness more important than validity alone?
faq.answer: Soundness guarantees both correct logic and true premises, meaning the conclusion must be true. Validity only checks structure, so it can produce elegant but false results.
